poc_summary: /poc/run.sh: build tests/modules/keyspace_events.so, start redis-server with it loaded, CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru, CONFIG SET maxmemory 1gb, CONFIG SET notify-keyspace-events 'A$', SET x 999999999, INCR x. Run via run_poc identically on pre_intro, post_intro, post_benign.
explanation: The module's KeySpace_NotificationModuleString handler (subscribed to REDISMODULE_NOTIFY_STRING) runs synchronously from notifyKeyspaceEvent() fired during INCR, and calls RedisModule_StringDMA on the key, which invokes dbUnshareStringValue()->dbSetValue(), freeing the 'new' robj that incrDecrCommand just stored as the key's value. In post_intro (05aed4cab976, PR #13505's optimization), incrDecrCommand replies via addReplyLongLongFromStr(c,new) AFTER signalModifiedKey()/notifyKeyspaceEvent() run, so it reads 'new's string buffer after it has been freed by this reentrant module callback. run_poc on post_intro reproduced exactly the upstream-reported AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free: addReply (networking.c:431) <- addReplyLongLongFromStr <- incrDecrCommand (t_string.c:607) <- incrCommand, freed by zfree<-decrRefCount<-dbSetValue<-dbUnshareStringValueWithDictEntry<-RM_StringDMA<-KeySpace_NotificationModuleString (tests/modules/keyspace_events.c:122) -- matching the frames in the GH-13875 report almost line-for-line. Using a large (non-shared-range) integer with maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru forces a real heap allocation (avoids the shared-integer pool that masked the bug previously, as the reporter noted) so the free is observable. The identical run.sh executed via run_poc against pre_intro (de7f2f87f74c, before the optimization) and post_benign (fix applied) both completed cleanly: INCR returned the correct value 1000000000, PING returned PONG, no sanitizer report, server stayed alive -- only post_intro crashed.
